newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma lashes out once more against Suu Kyi, U.S.
newsitem.headline: Burma lashes out once more against Suu Kyi, U.S.

text.p: Burma's state-run media on Tuesday lashed out at the United States for bullying weak countries and for exploiting democracy activist Aung San Suu Kyi, whom it said had no chance of ever becoming leader of Burma.

Commentaries published in all official Burmese newspapers said U.S. attacks on the human rights records of countries like Burma showed that Washington was continuing its policy of bullying the weak in pursuit of geopolitical hegemonism.
"The U.S., a superpower, has become a nation to be hated," the commentary said.

"The U.S. followed the words of its puppet and loyalist Daw Aung San Suu Kyi and bullied the weak," it said. "U.S. President Clinton and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright do not seem to possess mindfulness, sensibility and sympathy. They only listen to the exaggerated falsehood of Daw Aung San Suu Kyi."

The United States last month imposed economic sanctions banning new American investment in Burma because of Rangoon's human rights record and its failure to recognise the 1990 electoral victory of the National League for Democracy (NLD) party, led by Nobel Peace laureate Suu Kyi.

Since they released her from six years of house arrest in 1995, Burma has regularly accused Suu Kyi of colluding with the United States. Last week one of the country's top generals accused the NLD of accepting $85,200 from two covert U.S. agents earlier this year.
The United States has denied involvement.
The commentary also urged NLD members to question Suu Kyi's "submission to American influence."

"There are no prospects for Daw Aung San Suu Kyi to become a leader of Myanmar (Burma), or an opposition leader," it said. "For she has been committing one mistake after another. She has now taken steps to harm national interest."
"I would like to remind the NLD members to assess the woman's acts committed under the influence of her being...bent on destruction," it said. "The NLD will then be enslaved by the U.S. completely."
